pictures.title: Same Claude, different settings, different scores
pictures.data_source: Artificial Analysis, 15 Oct 2026
pictures.measures: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2: 10 hard tests, scored 0 to 100, higher is better. The dollar chips are its cost per task to run them, lower is cheaper.
pictures.card: Horizontal bars drawn from zero (ticks 0, 20, 40, 60), headed 'Scored 0 to 100. Higher is better.', and built in three steps on his three sentences. Step 1 ('In its top gear, it did much better'): Opus 5.5 at Low effort 42, Opus 5.5 at Max effort 58. Step 2 ('The older Opus 5, in its top gear'): add Opus 5 at Max effort 51, set against Opus 5.5 at Low 42. Step 3 ('To be fair, the new one's middle gear'): add Opus 5.5 at Medium effort 51, with cost chips: Opus 5.5 Medium $1.34 a task, Opus 5 Max $5.86 a task. Each effort shown as the chip label (LOW EFFORT, MEDIUM EFFORT, MAX EFFORT), never as a gear. Values from P1-02 (42, 51 at $1.34, 58) and its checker's matched-effort note (Opus 5 Max 50.8 at $5.86, shown as 51); the 90-second chart's 16 Oct API read gives the same 42 and 51.
pictures.start_long: A group called Artificial Analysis ran
pictures.end_long: top gear, for much less money.
pictures.evidence: evidence-v3.md P1-02 (lines 19-27: AA sentences for Low 42, Max 58, Opus 5 Max 51; medium page 51 at $1.34; checker's note: Opus 5.5 medium 51.2 at $1.34 matches Opus 5 max 50.8 at $5.86) and line 149
